references.text: The prophecy of the king coming to Zion, sitting on a donkey (v.9), which directly foretells the event in John 12:12 where the people meet Jesus on his way to Jerusalem.
The parallel account in Matthew about the large crowd spreading clothes and branches before Jesus, with the same theme of the people hearing about his arrival.
Mark's version of the entry, where a great multitude meets Jesus and hears that he is coming to Jerusalem, focusing on the public excitement.
Luke's account of the people spreading clothes on the road and shouting hallelujah, reflecting the action and atmosphere in John 12:12.
Psalm 118:26 contains the directly quoted greeting 'Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord', which the people shout in connection with Jesus' arrival in John 12:12.
